land.text: 'Around 1286, the Mali Empire conquered Takrur and put it under a military dictatorship ruled by farba (governors)'

successors.note: Cliopatria ends Takrur in 1235, when its Mali shape begins; the Takrur page dates the Mali conquest to c. 1285 (infobox) or around 1286 (text), so this dossier runs Takrur to 1285. The Jolof conquest of the 1450s (infobox 1456) and the Denianke kingdom of Futa Toro from 1513/1521 are later phases of the same land and need a dossier from the group's additions batch.

capitals.name: Takrur (seat uncertain; Tumbere Jiinge in the Gorgol valley)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Tumbere Jiinge (Dya'ogo, Manna dynasties), Taaga (Laam Taga), Hoorewendu (Laam Termess)'; the last two are Fula Laam-dynasty seats of later centuries. 'The Gorgol River valley was the heartland of the kingdom'; the page gives no coordinates, so the point is the centroid of the Cliopatria shape.

keyframe_review.note: 74,105 km2 along the Senegal River (16.6-11.7 W, 14.4-17.0 N): 'Takrur itself, however, extended across the river: its capital was situated on both banks of the Senegal'; Kane puts the cradle 'in the Senegal valley between Dagana and Dembankani'; the page adds that Takrur 'controlled, or at least had significant influence over, the area downstream that would become Waalo'. The infobox has no area, so no ratio. The shape's start (1040) is the death of War Jabi 'around 1040-1041' and the succession of Lebi; the state is older (infobox 'Established: 9th century'; 'as early as 100 CE' per Clark).

74,469 km2, 364 km2 more than the 1040 shape; the seed lists the Almoravid shape touching within 25 km from 1056 to 1138. The page records an alliance, not a border: Lebi 'would go on to start an alliance with the newly established Almoravid Dynasty' (infobox 'Alliance with the Almoravid Dynasty: c. 1050s'). No territorial change is dated at 1056, so the shape stands.

Back to 74,105 km2, the 1040 outline. The page says nothing of 1139; the 12th century on it is 'Silla, a vassal of Takrur, went to war against Wagadu' and a dominant position in regional trade. The shape stands.

correction.text: The Cliopatria 1227 shape unchanged, applied for 1227-1285

keyframe_review.note: Shape unchanged (74,105 km2, the Senegal valley), but the years should run 1227-1285 instead of 1227-1235: the page has Takrur independent until Mali 'around 1286' (infobox 'Conquered and vassalized by Mali Empire: c. 1285'), whereas Cliopatria folds the valley into its Mali shape from 1236. The Mali page's remark that Sundiata's generals reached 'Takrur, Oualata and Audaghost in the north' is undated and loses to the dated Takrur page.

region.text: the Senegal River valley with the Gorgol heartland

ledger.note: c. 1040: Takrur, the Senegal River kingdom that had adopted Sharia under War Jabi in 1035, passes to his son Lebi. The state is older than the map shows: infobox 'Established: 9th century', 'founded as early as 100 CE' (Clark), and a Soninke clan under Mamadu Sumaare 'conquered Takrur in the 9th or 10th century'; no page gives a year or a territory for the founding, so the map starts at Cliopatria's 1040 (War Jabi died 'around 1040-1041').

region.text: the Senegal River valley, Takrur's whole extent

ledger.note: c. 1285: Mali conquers Takrur. 'Around 1286, the Mali Empire conquered Takrur and put it under a military dictatorship ruled by farba (governors)'; infobox 'Conquered and vassalized by Mali Empire: c. 1285'. The year follows the infobox.

c. 1285: the last independent Takrur ends under Mali's farba governors. The land later passed to Jolof ('conquered Namandirou in approximately the 1450s, then extended his authority over Takrur', Jolof page; infobox 'Conquered by Jolof Empire: 1456') and in 1513/1521 to Koli Tenguella's Denianke.

wars.name: War Jabi's holy war against Silla
wars.outcome: No territorial result is recorded: 'During his reign he launched a Holy War against the King of Silla'.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the war inside War Jabi's reign (1035 Sharia, died c. 1040-41). Silla is later 'a vassal of Takrur' (12th century) according to the page.

wars.name: Mali conquest of Takrur
wars.outcome: Takrur became a Mali province under farba governors.
wars.note: Infobox c. 1285; text 'Around 1286'. The Mali page does not date it and says Sundiata's generals had reached Takrur earlier.

certainty.note: A river kingdom with fluid frontiers; the pages give no boundary. The Senegal valley itself is a natural axis.

sources.note: Identity, War Jabi and Lebi, the Almoravid alliance, the Mali conquest c. 1285/1286, capitals.

sources.title: Ghana Empire
sources.note: Oral tradition lists Takrur among Ghana's lands 'at its height'; the Takrur page does not.

notes: Cliopatria's four Takrur shapes (1040-1055, 1056-1138, 1139-1226, 1227-1235) are one outline of about 74,000 km2. Open points: (1) the dossier runs to 1285 instead of Cliopatria's 1235; the Mali dossier removes Takrur from its Cliopatria shape until 1285. The Mali page (Sundiata's generals reached Takrur) and the Takrur page (Mali conquered it around 1286) disagree; the dated page was followed. (2) The page's Takrur is a long-lived state (c. 500 / 9th century to 1456); only 1040-1285 is drawn. The Jolof (1450s/1456) and Denianke (1513/1521 to 1776) phases need a Futa Toro dossier. (3) Takrur as a Ghana tributary rests on the Ghana page's oral-tradition list only; the Takrur page says Lebi's Almoravid alliance was meant 'to counter the power of the Ghana Empire'. No vassal event is written. (4) Silla, 'a vassal of Takrur' in the 12th century, has no date or location on the page. (5) The page gives no ruler list with years; no ruler strip. (6) The Seshat page for Takrur was not tried (Takrur has no Seshat id); the Seshat page for Mali failed to load.
